title: Counting Days Late on Bank Deposit Transfers with a Hold History
content:
How late a Bank Deposit transfer was, for its late-delivery refund, depends on the transfer's hold history. The rule reads two things from the records: whether the transfer record shows a hold having been placed on the transfer (a moment a hold was placed is on record), and whether the transfer's case file carries any logged answer to a request for information, with the date each answer was logged.

## The rule

- **Hold placed, no answer logged.** When a hold was placed on the transfer and its case file carries no logged answer to a request for information, the days late are counted from the booking instead, as the calendar days from the date part of the booking moment to the deposit date less the tier's delivery business days.
- **Hold placed, answer logged.** When a hold was placed on the transfer and its case file carries a logged answer to a request for information, the days late are counted from the answer, as the calendar days from the latest answer's logged date to the deposit date less the tier's hold review business days and less the tier's delivery business days.
- **No hold ever placed.** A transfer on which no hold was ever placed is outside this rule.

## Tier figures the rule subtracts

| Tier | Delivery business days | Hold review business days |
|---|---|---|
| Bank Deposit Economy | 3 | 2 |
| Bank Deposit Standard | 1 | 2 |
| Bank Deposit Express | 0 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Express Plus | 0 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Large Amount | 1 | 3 |
| Bank Deposit International Wire | 2 | 3 |

## Input, judgement, output

| Hold on record? | Answer to a request for information logged? | Days late |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | calendar days from the booking date to the deposit date, less the delivery business days |
| yes | yes (one or more) | calendar days from the latest answer's logged date to the deposit date, less the hold review business days, less the delivery business days |
| no | (not read) | outside this rule |

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

1. **Bank Deposit Economy, held for partner screening, no answer logged.** Booked 2 March at 17:40, deposited 11 March. The booking date is 2 March; 2 March to 11 March is 9 calendar days; less 3 delivery business days gives 6 days late.
2. **Bank Deposit Standard, held for a request for information, answers logged on 4 March and 6 March.** Deposited 14 March. The latest answer was logged on 6 March; 6 March to 14 March is 8 calendar days; less 2 hold review business days and less 1 delivery business day gives 5 days late.
3. **Bank Deposit Express, held, one answer logged on 9 April.** Deposited 13 April: 4 calendar days, less 1 hold review business day and less 0 delivery business days, gives 3 days late.

## Questions the rule answers

**Several answers were logged on the case file. Which date counts?** The latest answer's logged date.

**The hold was released before the deposit. Does the release date matter?** No. The rule turns on whether a hold was placed and on the logged answers; the release date does not enter the count.
